title: The Tohoku-oki high-slip area b-value stayed 0.26 above its 1998-2011 level in 2016-2024 at JMA M 2.5 or more, while five other regions changed by 0.05 or less
abstract: Question: after the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-oki earthquake, did the b-value of the high-slip area stay at its 1998-2011 level? A 2015 study reported a quick return and used it as evidence of rapid stress recovery. Approach: we used the JMA unified hypocenter catalog for 1998-2024 (4.93 M events) in a high-slip box (37.5-39.0 N, 142.5-144.0 E, depth 60 km or less), two rupture-zone boxes and three control regions. We used Aki-Utsu b-values at fixed cutoffs, b-positive, a month-block bootstrap, step tests at 119 monthly dates, and GCMT faulting types. Result: in the high-slip area, b was 0.68 in 1998 to March 2011 and 0.93 in 2016-2024 at M 2.5 or more. The change was +0.26 (95% interval +0.18 to +0.33), and it was +0.27 at M 3.0 or more. The other regions changed by 0.05 or less, and the difference from the controls was +0.26 (+0.17 to +0.34). At M 3.0 or more, b was already 0.87 in 2013-2015. An apparent return in that window occurs only with a cutoff below completeness. At M 2.5 or more, b did not step when JMA added S-net seafloor stations on 1 September 2020. But b-positive had its largest step (+0.27) at that date in the high-slip area, and steps also occurred in the other S-net regions. Thus low-cutoff estimates offshore Tohoku are not stable across this processing change. M 4 or more events in the high-slip area fell to 1.6 per year in 2020-2024, against a median of 8 per year before 2011. GCMT had no Mw 5 or more events there in 2016-2020. Limitations: the box edges are approximate, the pre-2011 b-value was not constant, and against 1998-2001 only the change is +0.13 at M 2.5 and not clear at M 3.0. A changed source population can also explain a higher b-value, and this catalog cannot separate it from lower stress.

display.caption: a: Yearly b-values in the Tohoku-oki high-slip area at M 2.5 or more and M 3.0 or more, with 95% month-block bootstrap intervals. The band is the 1998-2011 value. Dotted lines show the mainshock and the two JMA processing changes. b: The 2016-2024 minus 1998-2011 b change in six regions.

a: High-slip area b-value against the cutoff magnitude in four periods. Before 2011 the curve is flat. After 2016 b is 0.9-1.0 above M 2.5 in both S-net periods. b: b in the two years after each test date minus b in the two years before. b-positive has its largest step at the S-net date (1 September 2020), but the M 2.5 estimate does not.

Yearly M 4 or more event counts in four Japan Trench regions, divided by the 1998-2010 yearly median. In 2020-2024 the high-slip area rate is below every pre-2011 year, while the north and south rupture zones are near or above their medians.

citations.reason: Reports a quick return of the high-slip b-value to pre-mainshock levels. We test whether the b-value stayed at that level through 2024.
Argues for slow reloading and for population effects on b. Our late high b-value agrees with this view.
